inputSnapshot.objective: Elite-style single-player space trading and combat game with a rich browser frontend played in Google Chrome. A local Node.js server serves the game; the player opens http://localhost:<port> in Chrome and plays immediately (npm install && npm start, no manual build steps). The frontend is a first-class acceptance subject: a beautiful single-page canvas/WebGL application with a parallax starfield, hyperspace jump effect, station docking screen, ship HUD (shields, fuel, cargo, credits), commodity market screen with dynamic prices, and arcade laser combat with visual effects. Core gameplay loop: start docked at a station with 100 credits and a small cargo hold; buy low / sell high across a galaxy of at least 8 named systems with per-system price variation; hyperspace jumps consume fuel and carry pirate-encounter risk; win ship-to-ship combat (player lasers vs enemy AI) or flee; spend profits on ship upgrades (cargo capacity, laser, shields, fuel tank); progress toward the Elite rating tracked by profit and combat kills; save/load the game state. Non-functional: 60fps target on a 2020 laptop in Chrome, no external CDN dependencies (fully offline), English UI. Testing: unit tests for market pricing, jump/fuel math, combat resolution and save/load; a browser smoke test that loads the page and asserts the canvas renders; the server must expose /healthz.

assumptions: Node.js (LTS) is the only runtime dependency; no Docker, no bundler, no external CDN
Browser target is Google Chrome on a 2020-era laptop
All game state is single-player; persistence via server-side file or browser localStorage, no database required
Canvas 2D is sufficient for visual effects; WebGL is optional for performance
The game is served as static assets by the Node.js server
npm test runs all unit tests; a separate smoke-test script covers the browser check
proposalPayload.candidate_scope: A Node.js HTTP server serving a single-page canvas/WebGL application. Features: galaxy of at least 8 named star systems with per-system commodity price variation, trading loop (buy low, sell high), hyperspace jumps consuming fuel with pirate-encounter risk, arcade ship-to-ship laser combat with enemy AI, ship upgrades (cargo capacity, laser, shields, fuel tank), Elite rating system tracked by profit and combat kills, save/load functionality, /healthz endpoint. Unit tests for market pricing, jump/fuel math, combat resolution, save/load. Browser smoke test verifying canvas rendering.
evidence_refs: initiative.objective: full game specification including gameplay loop, visual requirements, non-functional constraints, and testing requirements
proposalPayload.observed_context: Greenfield project (no existing code, artifacts, or notes). The repository is empty and the initiative was factory-started with a fully specified objective. Classified as XS complexity, type web-app. Runtime is Node.js serving a single-page application. Constraints: deployment excluded, local run required (npm install && npm start), human acceptance after local start in Chrome. No external CDN dependencies allowed (fully offline). The frontend is a first-class acceptance subject with specific visual requirements: parallax starfield, hyperspace jump effect, docking screen, ship HUD, commodity market, and arcade laser combat with visual effects.
proposalPayload.problem_statement: There is no single-player space trading and combat game that delivers a classic Elite-style experience playable immediately in a browser without build steps or CDN dependencies. Players who want a rich, immersive space trading experience must install native applications or rely on online services.
proposalPayload.rationale: The initiative is a well-specified, self-contained XS web-app with clear functional requirements, explicit non-functional constraints, and a bounded scope. All requirements are achievable with Node.js and vanilla browser APIs. The risks are technical implementation concerns (rendering performance, game balance), not feasibility blockers. No external dependencies, no deployment, and no multi-user concerns reduce complexity.
risks: Achieving 60fps canvas rendering with parallax starfield and combat effects on a 2020 laptop without a build step or framework
Balancing the trading economy across 8+ systems to make the buy-low/sell-high loop engaging
Implementing arcade combat with visual effects in a zero-build, no-framework frontend
Ensuring the browser smoke test is reliable across different Chrome versions
stakeholders_or_actors: Player: opens the game in Chrome, trades commodities, fights pirates, upgrades ship, pursues Elite rating
Factory operator: runs npm install && npm start locally and performs human acceptance in Chrome
unknowns: Exact canvas rendering approach (Canvas 2D vs. WebGL) for achieving 60fps on target hardware
Whether save/load should be file-based on the server or localStorage in the browser
The precise commodity set and galaxy map layout for balanced gameplay
The enemy AI difficulty curve and combat balance parameters
